evidence:
Scope: row 43 only. I used openpyxl on the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks row 44 and Internal Quality Checks row 44. The authoritative check requires gates to zero reward, skip the scored suite, carry no reward weight, and prevent presentation farming below the functional floor. The internal annotation says 'Gate/constraint failures hard-zero the quality terms, and passing only the cheap gates earns little.' I also inspected the same rows in the skill's assets/WebDev_Rubrics_QC.xlsx: the ZIP bytes differ between workbook copies, but these row contents are identical. The frozen skill, quality-checks.md section 43, staged-task-contract.md scoring/test.sh sections, deterministic-checks.md scoring-policy/canonical-shared-files sections and current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md were applied.

All task paths below are under .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/. tests/scoring.toml:1-11 has render=0.0 and constraints=0.0 under [gates], only functional=0.6/polish=0.2/visual=0.2 under [weights], and functional=0.05 under [floors]. Both gate judge.toml files:14-21 use all_pass and one binary criterion. Their criterion weight=1.0 is an internal all-pass aggregation weight, not reward mass: neither gate is in [weights]. All five judge.toml files parse, and none has [judge].weight. The policy, scorer and test.sh are individually byte-identical to their frozen template counterparts; no canonical-setting change is needed.

The relevant control flow is explicit. tests/test.sh:212 deletes stale scored results; :213 runs gates; :217 invokes score.py; :218-222 exits immediately on gate failure (status 1) or scoring error; only :224 then invokes the scored suite. tests/tools/score.py:40-44 requires every gate score to exceed its zero threshold and replaces all scored dimensions with 0 unless the gates pass and scored results exist. :46 sums only [weights]; :47 requires the functional score to be strictly above 0.05; :48 writes reward 0 unless both gates and floors pass; :83 returns 1 for gate failure. Thus a failed gate with even preexisting perfect scored input cannot contribute reward, and passing gates alone earns 0.

I directly executed the unmodified frozen score.py through the specified Python executable in disposable temporary log directories for eleven assertions. For render failure, constraints failure, and both failures, with functional/polish/visual all 1 in the supplied scored file, each run returned exit 1, reward=0, all scored dimensions=0 and four CTRF entries skipped. Gates-only input returned exit 0 with reward=0 and floors_passed=0. With both gates=1 and polish=visual=1, functional values 0, 0.049999 and 0.05 each produced reward=0 and floors_passed=0; functional=0.050001 produced reward=0.4300 and floors_passed=1, matching the canonical strict boundary. Fully conforming scores produced 1.0000; functional-only full credit produced 0.6000; functional=0.5, polish=0.25, visual=0.75 produced 0.5000. reward.json and reward.txt agreed in every case. These are actual local scorer executions with synthetic dimension inputs, not configured app-judge runs.

The gate wording supports the intended dead-app exclusion. tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25 requires a newly authored marker observed in both actual preview and console after Run, and rejects a no-op Run. tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29 requires a new successful UI save plus matching server-supplied identity and exact contents in an independent clean context and after its reload; localStorage, a static seed or a toast alone are insufficient. All three scored prompts restate a zeroing prerequisite (functional/prompt.md:5, polish/prompt.md:13-22, visual/prompt.md:24-33). The functional floor additionally prevents a zero-function but visually perfect result from earning the otherwise available 0.4. Its low canonical threshold intentionally permits reward once actual functional credit exceeds 0.05; that profile is not an invented defect.

Conforming-alternative challenge: a working server-rendered library with no separate JSON endpoint and a different usable control layout remains allowed by constraints/judge.toml:27 and all scored prerequisites. Missing Auto-run by itself cannot turn otherwise working Run/save into a gate failure because injected app_context.md:16 explicitly resolves that preparation instruction. Broken-alternative challenge: a polished editor with dead execution or browser-only fake saves fails the corresponding explicit gate; even if perfect presentation scores are supplied synthetically, the measured scorer output is 0. A both-gates-passed but functional=0 case also measured 0. No surviving false-pass or false-fail witness was established for this row.

I independently verified all 50 frozen task file hashes against manifest.json. score.py SHA256 is 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e; scoring.toml SHA256 is 95f70d6e06aae5e765b2309d88c444aa36d4cd82763ea2212781b6a99311bbba. raw-evidence-index.json explicitly records that the supplied golden evidence is direct scripted browser observation, with no full configured verifier, target model, Oracle or measured judge workload. I checked the raw RESULTS.json header and its indexed SHA256 ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09; it states paid_provider=false and direct pinned Playwright. I do not use that record as proof of configured judge gating or timing. The scorer arithmetic and source ordering are established here; a live complete configured-suite execution remains unmeasured, so run_verdict is PARTIAL rather than a claim of full runtime clearance.
